entities.name: Foodborne Trematodes
entities.description: A diverse group of zoonotic helminthic infections caused by digenetic flukes (liver flukes: Clonorchis, Opisthorchis, Fasciola; lung flukes: Paragonimus; intestinal flukes: Fasciolopsis, Heterophyes) acquired via ingestion of raw or undercooked freshwater fish, crustaceans, or aquatic plants.

entities.name: Biliary Colic
entities.description: Episodic, severe right upper quadrant or epigastric cramping pain resulting from mechanical irritation, obstruction, or migration of adult flukes within bile ducts.

entities.name: Acute Invasive Fascioliasis
entities.description: Acute clinical syndrome occurring during the 6 to 12 weeks of juvenile Fasciola migration through the peritoneal cavity and hepatic parenchyma.

entities.name: Chronic Biliary Fascioliasis
entities.description: Chronic hepatobiliary phase occurring when adult Fasciola flukes mature within major intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts, leading to biliary obstruction and fibrosis.

entities.name: Recurrent Pyogenic Cholangitis
entities.description: Repeated bacterial superinfections of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary tree associated with chronic Clonorchis sinensis or Opisthorchis viverrini colonization and biliary stasis.

entities.name: Cholangiocarcinoma
entities.description: Malignant neoplasm of the biliary epithelium strongly driven by chronic Clonorchis sinensis and Opisthorchis viverrini infection, recognized as an IARC Group 1 definitive biological carcinogen.

entities.name: Pulmonary Paragonimiasis
entities.description: Indolent pulmonary disease caused by Paragonimus flukes encapsulated in lung parenchyma, causing chronic cough, chest pain, and hemoptysis.

entities.name: Chocolate-Sauce Sputum Hemoptysis
entities.description: Pathognomonic expectoration of thick, brownish-rusty or gelatinous sputum composed of clotted blood, necrotic lung tissue, and masses of Paragonimus operculated eggs.

entities.name: Cerebral Paragonimiasis
entities.description: Severe extrapulmonary ectopic disease resulting from juvenile Paragonimus migration through the jugular foramen into the cranial cavity and brain parenchyma.

entities.name: Acalculous Cholecystitis
entities.description: Acute gallbladder inflammation in the absence of gallstones, induced by adult fluke migration, mechanical trauma, or mucosal irritation within the cystic duct and gallbladder.

entities.name: Secondary Biliary Cirrhosis
entities.description: End-stage chronic hepatic parenchymal destruction and micronodular cirrhosis secondary to protracted biliary obstruction and chronic periductal inflammation.

entities.name: Biliary Ductal Strictures
entities.description: Focal and segmental fibrous narrowing of the intrahepatic and common bile ducts caused by chronic fluke attachment, mechanical abrasion, and mucosal scarring.

entities.name: Intrahepatic Ductal Ectasia
entities.description: Saccular and diffuse dilation of the medium and small peripheral intrahepatic bile ducts upstream of fluke-induced mucosal inflammation and periductal fibrosis.

entities.name: Mechanical Biliary Obstruction
entities.description: Physical impaction of living adult flukes, dead worm remnants, and surrounding biliary sludge within the biliary tree leading to cholestasis and jaundice.

entities.name: Chronic Productive Cough
entities.description: Persistent, debilitating cough lasting months to years caused by the bronchial communication of Paragonimus cyst cavities in the lung parenchyma.

entities.name: Pleuritic Chest Pain
entities.description: Sharp, respiration-dependent thoracic pain caused by juvenile fluke penetration across the diaphragm and parietal pleura into the pleural space.

entities.name: Parasitic Pleural Effusion
entities.description: Accumulation of exudative, eosinophil-rich fluid within the pleural cavity triggered by migrating Paragonimus larvae crossing pleural surfaces.

entities.name: Spontaneous Pneumothorax
entities.description: Acute accumulation of air in the pleural cavity caused by the rupture of subpleural necrotic Paragonimus cysts into the pleural space.

entities.name: Extrapulmonary Ectopic Paragonimiasis
entities.description: Aberrant larval migration of Paragonimus juvenile flukes into non-pulmonary tissues including the brain, spinal cord, abdominal wall, and scrotum.

entities.name: Subcutaneous Migratory Nodules
entities.description: Painful, pruritic, slow-moving subcutaneous swellings and inflammatory nodules produced by aberrantly migrating flukes in the subcutaneous fat and connective tissue.

entities.name: Ectopic Hepatic Migration
entities.description: Aberrant tracking of Paragonimus larvae through the liver capsule and parenchyma prior to breaching the diaphragm into the thoracic cavity.

entities.name: Intestinal Fasciolopsiasis
entities.description: Intestinal mucosal infection caused by the giant intestinal fluke Fasciolopsis buski adhering to the duodenal and jejunal mucosa.

entities.name: Chronic Mucous Diarrhea
entities.description: Frequent, loose, mucus-laden stools caused by extensive mechanical attachment and toxic secretome of intestinal flukes like Fasciolopsis buski and Heterophyes heterophyes.

entities.name: Protein-Losing Enteropathy
entities.description: Profound enteric loss of serum proteins across ulcerated, inflamed intestinal mucosa colonized by giant intestinal flukes.

entities.name: Periductal Fibrosis
entities.description: Concentric, dense fibrous thickening of the peribiliary stroma and intrahepatic connective tissue sheath induced by chronic fluke mechanical injury and secretome.

entities.name: Biliary Epithelial Hyperplasia
entities.description: Marked adenomatous proliferation, mucinous metaplasia, and goblet cell hyperplasia of the bile duct epithelial lining exposed to chronic liver fluke contact.

entities.name: Suppurative Bacterial Cholangitis
entities.description: Acute life-threatening purulent bacterial infection of the biliary conduits occurring when fluke-induced ductal obstruction facilitates rapid enteric bacterial multiplication.

entities.name: Hepatic Parenchymal Burrows
entities.description: Linear and serpentine necrotic hemorrhagic tracks created mechanically by juvenile Fasciola flukes tunneling through the liver parenchyma toward bile ducts.

entities.name: Glisson Capsule Perforation
entities.description: Direct mechanical puncture and erosion of the hepatic peritoneal covering (Glisson capsule) by migrating juvenile Fasciola flukes crossing from the peritoneum.

entities.name: Adult-Onset Parasitic Epilepsy
entities.description: New-onset focal or generalized seizures in an adult resident of an endemic region, triggered by intracranial Paragonimus fluke granulomas.

entities.name: Intracranial Space-Occupying Lesions
entities.description: Intracerebral granulomatous masses and cystic nodules produced by Paragonimus flukes, provoking intracranial hypertension.

entities.name: Intracerebral Hemorrhage
entities.description: Cerebral parenchymal bleeding resulting from parasite erosion of intracranial blood vessels or surrounding necrotic cavitation during cerebral paragonimiasis.

entities.name: Heterophyid Cardiac Embolization
entities.description: Aberrant hematogenous dissemination of minute Heterophyes or Metagonimus eggs into coronary vessels and myocardium, causing parasitic myocarditis.

entities.name: Spinal Cord Paragonimiasis
entities.description: Extradural or subdural granulomatous fluke lesions in the spinal canal producing progressive spinal cord compression and myelopathy.

entities.name: Eosinophilic Peritonitis
entities.description: Peritoneal exudative inflammation with abundant eosinophils caused by juvenile Fasciola flukes actively transiting across the peritoneal cavity.

entities.name: Hepatic Subcapsular Hematoma
entities.description: Subcapsular accumulation of blood beneath Glisson's capsule resulting from extensive parenchymal burrowing and laceration of intrahepatic microvessels.

entities.name: Acute Cholecystitis Mimic
entities.description: Severe episodic right upper quadrant pain, Murphy-like tenderness, and fever mimicking acute calculus cholecystitis, caused by fluke impaction in the cystic duct.

entities.name: Recurrent Pancreatitis
entities.description: Episodes of acute pancreatic inflammation triggered by fluke migration into the ampulla of Vater or main pancreatic duct.

entities.name: Biliary Microabscesses
entities.description: Multiple small parenchymal and periductal suppurative microabscesses developing along obstructed, colonized intrahepatic biliary branches.

entities.name: Chronic Cachexia
entities.description: Profound systemic wasting, muscle loss, and chronic asthenia resulting from long-standing biliary inflammation, anorexia, and malabsorption.

entities.name: Severe Anasarca
entities.description: Generalized, massive soft-tissue edema and third-space fluid accumulation resulting from extreme hypoalbuminemia in intestinal fluke disease.

entities.name: Rusty Sputum Expectoration
entities.description: Physical expectoration of viscous, chocolate-brown to rusty sputum containing blood, Charcot-Leyden crystals, and operculated eggs, pathognomonic of pulmonary paragonimiasis.

entities.name: Tender Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Enlarged, tender liver palpable below the right costal margin resulting from intense parenchymal inflammation, burrowing tracks, or biliary distension.

entities.name: Right Upper Quadrant Tenderness
entities.description: Exquisite focal tenderness on deep palpation over the right hypochondrium corresponding to Glisson capsule stretching or biliary inflammation.

entities.name: Intermittent Jaundice
entities.description: Fluctuating icterus of the skin and mucous membranes reflecting transient mechanical obstruction of major bile ducts by migrating flukes or biliary sludge.

entities.name: Urticarial Allergic Rash
entities.description: Pruritic, transient erythematous wheals and hives triggered by systemic hypersensitivity reactions to migrating fluke excretory-secretory antigens.

entities.name: Facial Angioedema
entities.description: Episodic, non-pitting edema of the periorbital and facial soft tissues caused by acute IgE-mediated hypersensitivity to circulating parasite antigens.

entities.name: Crepitant Pulmonary Rales
entities.description: Auscultatory crackles and crepitations over mid- and lower lung zones indicating alveolar inflammation and fluid surrounding fluke cavitary lesions.

entities.name: Decreased Breath Sounds
entities.description: Diminished vesicular breath sounds on auscultation over thoracic regions affected by parasitic pleural effusion or pleural thickening.

entities.name: Dullness to Percussion
entities.description: Stony percussion dullness over dependent hemithoraces indicating moderate to large exudative parasitic pleural fluid collections.

entities.name: Pleural Friction Rub
entities.description: Grating auscultatory sound heard during inspiration and expiration reflecting direct mechanical friction between inflamed, roughened pleural surfaces.

entities.name: Subcutaneous Crepitant Swellings
entities.description: Subcutaneous, doughy or crepitant migratory soft-tissue nodules that change anatomical location over days, pathognomonic of ectopic fluke tracking.

entities.name: Focal Neurological Deficits
entities.description: Hemiparesis, localized motor weakness, or sensory loss caused by cerebral fluke granulomas compressing cortical and subcortical pathways.

entities.name: Papilledema on Fundoscopy
entities.description: Bilateral optic disc swelling with blurred margins observed on ophthalmoscopy, indicating chronic intracranial hypertension from cerebral granulomas.

entities.name: Meningismus and Photophobia
entities.description: Nuchal rigidity, Kernig sign, and marked light sensitivity reflecting intense meningeal inflammation triggered by subarachnoid fluke antigens.

entities.name: Tender Epigastric Mass
entities.description: Palpable, ill-defined tender inflammatory mass in the epigastrium or left lobe of the liver representing confluent fluke burrows or omental wrapping.

entities.name: Palpable Distended Gallbladder
entities.description: Enlarged, smooth, tense gallbladder palpable in the right hypochondrium (Courvoisier-like sign) resulting from distal common bile duct fluke obstruction.

entities.name: Ascites With Shifting Dullness
entities.description: Demonstrable abdominal fluid shift and fluid wave indicating exudative eosinophilic ascites or secondary decompensation in biliary cirrhosis.

entities.name: Spiking High Fever
entities.description: High continuous or intermittent fevers reaching 39 to 40 degrees Celsius accompanied by shaking chills during acute fluke tissue invasion or cholangitis.

entities.name: Persistent Biliary Colic
entities.description: Unrelenting, severe right hypochondrial spasms and pain unresponsive to simple antispasmodics, caused by active fluke muscular contractions within bile ducts.

entities.name: Scleral Icterus
entities.description: Yellowish pigmentation of the sclerae detectable when serum total bilirubin exceeds 2.5 to 3.0 mg/dL due to biliary outflow obstruction.

entities.name: Excoriations From Pruritus
entities.description: Linear scratch marks and skin abrasions secondary to intense generalized pruritus provoked by circulating bile salts and parasite antigens.

entities.name: Peripheral Pitting Edema
entities.description: Bilateral lower extremity edema that pits on pressure, caused by marked hypoalbuminemia resulting from intestinal fluke malabsorption.

entities.name: Abdominal Distension
entities.description: Diffuse swelling of the abdomen with tympany or fluid waves resulting from paralytic ileus, bowel wall edema, or eosinophilic ascites.

entities.name: Cachectic Temporal Wasting
entities.description: Loss of bitemporal fat pads and prominent facial bone contours indicating advanced protein-calorie malnutrition in long-standing disease.

entities.name: Halitosis With Putrid Sputum
entities.description: Offensive, foul breath odor accompanying copious expectoration of necrotic brownish sputum from long-standing secondarily infected lung fluke cysts.

entities.name: Hyperactive Bowel Sounds
entities.description: Frequent, loud, high-pitched borborygmi heard throughout the abdomen reflecting intestinal hypermotility and mucosal irritation.

entities.name: Cervical Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Enlarged, firm, non-tender or mildly tender lymph nodes in the anterior and posterior cervical triangles responding to upper respiratory and pleural inflammation.

entities.name: Splenomegaly on Palpation
entities.description: Palpable enlargement of the spleen below the left costal margin secondary to reticuloendothelial hyperplasia or non-cirrhotic portal hypertension.

entities.name: Extreme Peripheral Eosinophilia
entities.description: Profound elevation of absolute eosinophil count (often >40-80% of differential, absolute count 10,000-35,000/uL), universal in acute invasive trematodiasis.

entities.name: Elevated Alkaline Phosphatase
entities.description: Marked elevation of serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP >3-5x ULN) reflecting intense chronic biliary epithelial irritation and cholestasis.

entities.name: Marked GGT Elevation
entities.description: Substantial rise in serum gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT >4-6x ULN) confirming biliary epithelial injury and cholestatic stress.

entities.name: Elevated Serum IgE
entities.description: Astronomical elevation of total serum immunoglobulin E (frequently >1,000-5,000 IU/mL) provoked by strong Th2 immune responses to fluke antigens.

entities.name: Direct Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Predominant elevation of conjugated bilirubin (direct bilirubin >2.0 mg/dL) reflecting mechanical bile duct occlusion by adult flukes or ductal strictures.

entities.name: Mild Transaminitis
entities.description: Mild to moderate elevations of serum AST and ALT (2-4x ULN) reflecting parenchymal hepatocellular necrosis during larval burrowing or secondary cholangitis.

entities.name: Marked Leukocytosis
entities.description: Elevated total white blood cell count (WBC 15,000-40,000/uL) driven primarily by massive absolute eosinophilia and reactive neutrophilia.

entities.name: Elevated C-Reactive Protein
entities.description: High serum CRP levels (>50-100 mg/L) indicating active acute-phase systemic inflammation during fluke tissue migration and secondary cholangitis.

entities.name: Elevated Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate
entities.description: Significantly accelerated ESR (>60-100 mm/hr) resulting from intense polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia and systemic inflammation.

entities.name: Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
entities.description: Decreased hemoglobin and hematocrit with low MCV and MCH resulting from chronic gastrointestinal blood loss, hemoptysis, or bone marrow suppression.

entities.name: Branching Subcapsular Hepatic Tracks
entities.description: Linear, branching, serpentine hypoechoic or hypodense parenchymal tunnels ('tunnels and burrows') on ultrasound and CT, pathognomonic of migrating Fasciola flukes.

entities.name: Peripheral Intrahepatic Ductal Dilation
entities.description: Diffuse, uniform, non-tapering dilation of peripheral intrahepatic bile ducts with normal extrahepatic ducts on ultrasound/CT, pathognomonic of clonorchiasis.

entities.name: Increased Periductal Echogenicity
entities.description: Thickened, brightly hyperechoic cuffs encircling intrahepatic bile ducts on abdominal ultrasound, representing periductal collagenous fibrosis.

entities.name: Mobile Gallbladder Sludge
entities.description: Floating, non-shadowing echogenic material within the gallbladder lumen that shifts with patient repositioning, representing living flukes and desquamated mucosa.

entities.name: Acalculous Biliary Sludge
entities.description: Accumulation of echogenic particulate matter in bile ducts without acoustic shadowing or true stone formation, causing mechanical ductal distension.

entities.name: Ring-Shadow Pulmonary Cavities
entities.description: Thin- or thick-walled round cystic lesions (1-3 cm) with surrounding ground-glass opacity on chest radiograph, pathognomonic of pulmonary paragonimiasis.

entities.name: Migratory Pulmonary Infiltrates
entities.description: Patchy, non-segmental alveolar consolidations and nodular opacities on serial chest X-rays that spontaneously shift anatomical location over weeks.

entities.name: Multilocular Soap-Bubble Brain Calcifications
entities.description: Clustered, round, calcified multilocular cystic lesions resembling soap bubbles on head CT, pathognomonic of chronic cerebral paragonimiasis.

entities.name: Exudative Eosinophilic Pleural Fluid
entities.description: Thoracentesis fluid demonstrating high protein, elevated LDH, and marked eosinophil predominance (>10-50% of nucleated cells) with Charcot-Leyden crystals.

entities.name: Pleural Fluid Low Glucose
entities.description: Markedly depressed glucose concentration (<10-60 mg/dL) in pleural effusion fluid resulting from intense local parasite metabolism and cellular turnover.

entities.name: Operculated Eggs in Sputum
entities.description: Golden-brown, thick-shelled operculated eggs measuring 80-120 um by 45-65 um with a prominent opercular rim, definitive on unstained sputum wet mounts.

entities.name: Pitcher-Shaped Operculated Stool Eggs
entities.description: Small, yellowish-brown operculated eggs measuring 25-35 um by 12-19 um with an expanded shoulder collar and tiny abopercular knob, diagnostic of Clonorchis/Opisthorchis.

entities.name: Large Unembryonated Operculated Eggs
entities.description: Large, golden-yellow unembryonated operculated eggs measuring 130-150 um by 65-90 um detected in feces or duodenal aspirate, diagnostic of Fasciola/Fasciolopsis.

entities.name: Positive Fasciola Coproantigen ELISA
entities.description: Detection of Fasciola excretory-secretory antigens in stool using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, positive weeks before microscopic egg shedding.

entities.name: Serum IgG Parasite Antibodies
entities.description: High titers of parasite-specific IgG antibodies detected by ELISA against excretory-secretory fluke antigens, highly sensitive during acute invasive disease.

entities.name: Charcot-Leyden Sputum Crystals
entities.description: Slender, hexagonal bipyramidal crystals derived from eosinophil lysophospholipase breakdown, abundant in sputum wet mounts.

entities.name: Subcapsular Hepatic Hypodense Clusters
entities.description: Clustered or branching hypodense lesions in the peripheral subcapsular liver parenchyma on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT during acute invasion.

entities.name: Normal Extrahepatic Bile Duct
entities.description: Preservation of normal common bile duct caliber (<6-7 mm) despite marked peripheral intrahepatic duct dilatation, characteristic of Clonorchis infection.

entities.name: Thickened Gallbladder Wall
entities.description: Diffuse gallbladder wall thickening (>3 mm) without gallstones on abdominal ultrasound, indicating chronic fluke cholecystitis.

entities.name: Pleural Thickening and Blunting
entities.description: Blunting of the costophrenic sulcus and pleural rind formation on chest radiography resulting from chronic Paragonimus pleurisy.

entities.name: Linear Tunnel Ultrasound Lesions
entities.description: Serpentine, branching hypoechoic linear parenchymal tracks visible on bedside liver ultrasound representing active mechanical larval burrows.

entities.name: Intracranial Ring-Enhancing Nodules
entities.description: Multiple round or conglomerate ring-enhancing granulomatous nodules with surrounding vasogenic edema on contrast brain MRI.

entities.name: Periventricular White Matter Edema
entities.description: Extensive hyperintense T2/FLAIR signal abnormalities in periventricular white matter surrounding cerebral fluke lesions.

entities.name: Eosinophilic Ascitic Fluid
entities.description: Paracentesis revealing peritoneal exudate with marked eosinophilia (>10-40% of leukocytes) during acute peritoneal migration.

entities.name: Serum Amylase and Lipase
entities.description: Acute elevations of serum pancreatic enzymes (amylase and lipase >3x ULN) resulting from fluke impaction at the pancreatic ampullary sphincter.

entities.name: Hypoalbuminemia
entities.description: Severe depression of serum albumin (<2.5-3.0 g/dL) resulting from mucosal ulceration, lymphatic weeping, and protein-losing enteropathy.

entities.name: Elevated CA19-9 Tumor Marker
entities.description: Marked elevation of serum carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (>100-1,000 U/mL) in patients with liver fluke-associated cholangiocarcinoma.

entities.name: Kato-Katz Microscopic Stool Smear
entities.description: Standard quantitative parasitological thick smear revealing characteristic operculated eggs per gram of feces for disease staging.

entities.name: Raw Freshwater Cyprinid Fish
entities.description: Dietary ingestion of raw, pickled, fermented, or undercooked freshwater carp or cyprinid fish harboring encysted metacercariae of Clonorchis sinensis or Opisthorchis species.

entities.name: Raw Freshwater Crustaceans
entities.description: Consumption of raw, undercooked, salted, wine-soaked, or marinated freshwater river crabs or crayfish harboring encysted Paragonimus metacercariae.

entities.name: Raw Watercress Ingestion
entities.description: Ingestion of unwashed wild aquatic watercress (Nasturtium officinale) harboring encysted Fasciola metacercariae attached to stems and leaves.

entities.name: Raw Water Spinach Ingestion
entities.description: Consumption of raw, unwashed aquatic plants such as water spinach, water caltrops, or water chestnuts bearing Fasciola or Fasciolopsis metacercariae.

entities.name: Untreated Surface Grazing Water
entities.description: Drinking unboiled surface water or canal water in pastoral areas contaminated with floating Fasciola metacercariae detached from vegetation.

entities.name: Raw Paratenic Wild Boar
entities.description: Consumption of raw or undercooked meat from paratenic mammalian hosts such as wild boars that harbor viable Paragonimus juvenile larvae in muscle tissue.

entities.name: Freshwater Aquatic Snail Habitats
entities.description: Proximity to freshwater bodies harboring specific hydrobiid, bithyniid, or lymnaeid snails serving as mandatory first intermediate hosts.

entities.name: Endemic East Asian Residence
entities.description: Residence in or travel to highly endemic foci of Clonorchis sinensis in China, South Korea, northern Vietnam, and far eastern Russia.

entities.name: Lower Mekong Basin Resident
entities.description: Residence along the Mekong river basin in northeast Thailand, Laos, or Cambodia with hyperendemic Opisthorchis viverrini transmission.

entities.name: Andean Highlands Pastoralist
entities.description: Inhabitants of high-altitude pastoral valleys in Bolivia and Peru where human fascioliasis hyperendemicity reaches up to 70% in school-age children.

entities.name: Sheep and Cattle Husbandry
entities.description: Occupational engagement in raising ruminant livestock (sheep, goats, cattle) that serve as primary definitive reservoir hosts for Fasciola hepatica.

entities.name: Consumption of Thai Koi-Pla
entities.description: Traditional cultural consumption of raw, spiced freshwater fish salad (koi pla) in northeast Thailand, driving intense Opisthorchis transmission.

entities.name: Chinese Drunken Crab Dishes
entities.description: Traditional culinary ingestion of live freshwater river crabs steeped in rice wine or brine without thermal cooking, harboring Paragonimus metacercariae.

entities.name: Fish-Eating Carnivore Reservoir
entities.description: Sympatric populations of wild carnivores (otters, badgers, minks) maintaining zoonotic transmission cycles of liver and lung flukes.

entities.name: Canine and Feline Reservoirs
entities.description: Domestic dogs and cats that consume raw fish and crab waste, shedding viable trematode eggs into community waterways.

entities.name: Freshwater Aquaculture Workers
entities.description: Fish farmers and fish processing workers handling untreated freshwater aquaculture ponds fertilized with untreated human or animal manure.

entities.name: Acute Fascioliasis Incubation Period
entities.description: Incubation timeline of 1 to 6 weeks post-ingestion before acute hepatic migration symptoms emerge, followed by patency at 3 to 4 months.

entities.name: Chronic Clonorchiasis Incubation Period
entities.description: Incubation period of 3 to 4 weeks to egg patency, with clinical cholangiopathy and carcinogenesis evolving insidiously over 10 to 30 years.

entities.name: Paragonimiasis Incubation Period
entities.description: Incubation latency of 2 to 12 weeks from raw crustacean ingestion to pulmonary cyst formation, with adult worms surviving up to 20 years.

entities.name: Inadequate Food Thermal Processing
entities.description: Culinary practices utilizing smoking, pickling, salting, or drying without boiling or thorough cooking, failing to inactivate encysted metacercariae.

entities.name: Substandard Agricultural Sanitation
entities.description: Use of night soil (untreated human feces) as fertilizer in freshwater fish ponds and aquatic vegetable patches, perpetuating transmission.

entities.name: Raw Wild Vegetable Foraging
entities.description: Foraging and consuming wild freshwater greens, marsh grasses, or wild watercress from pastures grazed by livestock.

entities.name: Absent Peripheral Eosinophilia
entities.description: Normal peripheral blood eosinophil count (<3% or <500/uL) during an acute febrile hepatic or pulmonary illness, strongly excluding acute fluke invasion.

entities.name: Zero Dietary Freshwater Exposure
entities.description: Complete lifelong absence of consumption of raw or undercooked freshwater fish, crustaceans, aquatic vegetables, or unboiled grazing surface water.

entities.name: Acute Rice-Water Watery Diarrhea
entities.description: Profuse, voluminous, non-inflammatory secretory watery diarrhea without eosinophilia, characteristic of Vibrio cholerae.

entities.name: High Procalcitonin Sepsis Syndrome
entities.description: Hyperacute septic shock with procalcitonin >10 ng/mL and prominent neutrophilic left shift without eosinophilia, indicating fulminant bacterial sepsis.

entities.name: Massive Acid-Fast Bacilli Smear
entities.description: Strongly positive sputum smear for acid-fast bacilli (3+ or 4+ AFB) or positive GeneXpert MTB/RIF in a patient with cavitary lung disease.

entities.name: Rapid Response to Ceftriaxone
entities.description: Prompt clinical defervescence and complete resolution of hepatic or pulmonary infiltrates within 48 to 72 hours of starting third-generation cephalosporins.

entities.name: Solitary Liquefactive Amebic Cavity
entities.description: Demonstration of a solitary large round liquefactive hepatic cavity with anchovy-paste aspirate and positive Entamoeba histolytica serology.

entities.name: Normal Serum Alkaline Phosphatase
entities.description: Completely normal serum alkaline phosphatase and GGT in a patient with suspected long-standing chronic liver fluke infection.

entities.name: Acalculous Cholecystectomy Cure
entities.description: Complete curative resolution of biliary pain following cholecystectomy with pathology showing uncomplicated acalculous cholecystitis devoid of flukes or eggs.

entities.name: Strict Urban Cooked Diet
entities.description: Strict dietary adherence to thoroughly boiled, commercially prepared food without any raw freshwater products in a non-endemic metropolis.

entities.name: Pure Segmental Pneumonic Consolidation
entities.description: Dense, homogeneous lobar or segmental consolidation with air bronchograms resolving rapidly on ampicillin-sulbactam.

entities.name: Non-Eosinophilic Sputum Purulence
entities.description: Expectoration of yellow-green purulent sputum containing exclusively degenerate neutrophils and bacterial cocci without Charcot-Leyden crystals or eggs.

entities.name: Negative Clonorchis Coproantigen Test
entities.description: Repeatedly negative enzyme immunoassay for Clonorchis or Opisthorchis coproantigen alongside negative concentrated stool egg examinations.

entities.name: Zero Hepatic Parenchymal Lesions
entities.description: Completely normal triphasic contrast abdominal CT and ultrasound showing pristine liver parenchyma without tunnels, burrows, or ductal dilatation.

entities.name: High-Grade Neutrophilic Leukemoid Reaction
entities.description: WBC >35,000/uL with >90% toxic granulated neutrophils and zero eosinophils, indicating severe pyogenic bacterial infection or leukemoid reaction.

entities.name: Rapid Defervescence on Chloroquine
entities.description: Complete defervescence and parasite clearance within 24 to 48 hours of starting antimalarial therapy, confirming Plasmodium infection.

entities.name: Absence of Snail Habitats
entities.description: Lifelong residence in arid desert or alpine environments lacking freshwater snail intermediate hosts and aquatic food chains.

entities.name: Isolated Unconjugated Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Elevated total bilirubin with normal direct fraction (<15%), normal ALP, normal GGT, and normal transaminases, indicating Gilbert syndrome or hemolysis.

entities.name: Persistent Symptoms After Triclabendazole
entities.description: Lack of clinical, radiologic, or eosinophilic improvement after two adequate weight-based doses of triclabendazole in a patient suspected of fascioliasis.

entities.name: Normal Total Serum IgE
entities.description: Serum total IgE levels strictly within normal baseline reference limits (<20-50 IU/mL) during acute invasive multi-organ symptoms.

entities.name: Hyperacute Neurological Coma
entities.description: Sudden catastrophic loss of consciousness within minutes to hours without antecedent headaches or pulmonary symptoms, indicating acute thromboembolism.

entities.name: Negative Parasite Wet Mount
entities.description: Repeatedly negative direct microscopic wet mounts and formal concentration exams of sputum and stool in a patient with chronic respiratory complaints.

entities.name: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
entities.description: Chronic granulomatous mycobacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, presenting with cough, fever, cavitations, and hemoptysis.

entities.name: Amebic Liver Abscess
entities.description: Suppurative hepatic cavity caused by Entamoeba histolytica presenting with right upper quadrant pain, high fever, and liquefactive necrosis.

entities.name: Choledocholithiasis
entities.description: Calculus obstruction of the common bile duct causing biliary colic, jaundice, and potential ascending cholangitis.

entities.name: Acute Viral Hepatitis
entities.description: Hepatotropic viral infection (HAV, HBV, HCV, HEV) causing diffuse hepatocellular necrosis, profound transaminitis, and jaundice.

entities.name: Schistosomiasis
entities.description: Waterborne blood fluke infection acquired via percutaneous penetration of cercariae, causing urogenital or intestinal/hepatosplenic disease.

entities.name: Pyogenic Liver Abscess
entities.description: Bacterial collection in hepatic parenchyma causing fever, septic leukocytosis, and right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness.

entities.name: Echinococcosis
entities.description: Larval cestode infection caused by Echinococcus granulosus or multilocularis forming well-defined hydatid cysts in the liver and lungs.

entities.name: Ascariasis
entities.description: Large intestinal nematode infection caused by Ascaris lumbricoides, with larvae migrating through lungs and adult worms invading bile ducts.

entities.name: Bacterial Cholangitis
entities.description: Acute infection of the biliary conduits classically manifesting as Charcot triad (RUQ pain, jaundice, fever) and septic shock.

entities.name: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
entities.description: Chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by progressive inflammation and obliterative fibrosis of intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts.

entities.name: Neurocysticercosis
entities.description: Central nervous system infection caused by the larval stage of the pork tapeworm Taenia solium, causing seizures and cystic brain lesions.

entities.name: Lung Adenocarcinoma
entities.description: Primary malignant epithelial tumor of the lung arising from bronchial mucous glands, presenting with cough, hemoptysis, and peripheral nodules.

entities.name: Celiac Disease
entities.description: Autoimmune enteropathy triggered by dietary gluten ingestion leading to villous atrophy, chronic diarrhea, and malabsorption.

entities.name: Strongyloidiasis
entities.description: Intestinal nematode infection caused by Strongyloides stercoralis capable of autoinfection and persistent larval cutaneous migration.

entities.name: Loeffler Syndrome
entities.description: Transient pulmonary eosinophilia caused by transpulmonary larval migration of nematodes such as Ascaris or hookworms.

entities.name: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
entities.description: Primary malignancy of hepatocytes arising almost exclusively in the setting of chronic cirrhosis, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C.

entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: Zoonotic spirochetal infection presenting with biphasic high fever, conjunctival suffusion, acute kidney injury, and jaundice (Weil disease).

entities.name: Chronic Pancreatitis
entities.description: Progressive fibro-inflammatory disease of the pancreas causing permanent morphological damage, pain, and loss of exocrine/endocrine function.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Foodborne trematodiasis is differentiated from primary sclerosing cholangitis by uniform non-tapering peripheral intrahepatic ductal dilation without multifocal 'beading', absence of ulcerative colitis, and cure with anthelmintics.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Foodborne trematodiasis is differentiated from neurocysticercosis by clustered multilocular calcified lesions showing the 'soap-bubble' sign on CT and concomitant pulmonary cystic lesions with operculated eggs.

relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Foodborne trematodiasis is differentiated from lung adenocarcinoma by younger patient age, marked peripheral eosinophilia, raw crab ingestion, operculated eggs in sputum, and complete resolution following praziquantel therapy.

relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Foodborne trematodiasis is differentiated from celiac disease by presence of large operculated Fasciolopsis eggs in stool, negative anti-tTG antibodies, prominent eosinophilia, and rapid cure with praziquantel.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Foodborne trematodiasis is differentiated from strongyloidiasis by detection of operculated trematode eggs rather than motile rhabditiform larvae in stool, and primary hepatobiliary or pulmonary parenchymal localization.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Foodborne trematodiasis is differentiated from Loeffler syndrome by chronic, permanent cavitary lung lesions and recurrent hemoptysis lasting years, unlike the benign self-limited (1-2 week) pulmonary infiltrates of Loeffler syndrome.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Foodborne trematodiasis-associated cholangiocarcinoma is differentiated from hepatocellular carcinoma by normal alpha-fetoprotein, marked CA19-9 elevation, delayed peripheral enhancement on CT, and intrahepatic bile duct origin.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Foodborne trematodiasis is differentiated from leptospirosis by prominent peripheral eosinophilia (>40%), subcapsular liver burrow tracks, normal renal function, and absence of conjunctival suffusion.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Foodborne trematodiasis is differentiated from chronic calcific pancreatitis by characteristic peripheral intrahepatic ductal ectasia, stool fluke eggs, peripheral eosinophilia, and relief following anthelmintic therapy.
